lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Put Mobility Systems Company before Eastern Robotics Co.
items.because: The experience section should be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Clarify whether the internship was part-time, full-time, or a co-op.
items.because: It overlaps with the master’s program and could raise schedule questions.

items.says: Consider putting experience before education for experienced software roles.
items.because: Experience may be the stronger first section for those applications.

items.says: Standardize country and location formatting across education and experience.
Use en dashes consistently for all date ranges.
The current line break splitting “on-call” after “on-” looks like a formatting error.
Reduce the six highly technical bullets in the internship section.
items.because: They are difficult to scan, so the strongest production, quality, and latency achievements should be prioritized.

items.says: Make bullet lengths more uniform.
items.because: Several bullets span four or more lines and contain multiple accomplishments.

items.says: Make the code or portfolio URL clickable and link it directly to polished, relevant work.
Identify the URL clearly if it is GitHub.
items.because: The reader should not have to infer what the link contains.

items.says: Add LinkedIn if it is complete and consistent with the résumé.
Consider adding current location or work authorization.
items.because: Either may help employers understand availability.

items.says: Confirm that “Expected Jun 2026” matches the university’s official expected completion date.
Consider including GPA if it is strong and useful for the targeted roles.
Clarify what “owned” involved, such as development, maintenance, alert design, incident response, or operational accountability.
Add an outcome such as reduced detection time, fewer missed incidents, or improved response time.
Describe the actual operational responsibility instead of saying you “owned the on-call rotation.”
items.because: The current wording is imprecise.

items.says: Keep the two-release scope only if “major releases” has a meaningful definition.
Clarify the test environment or production traffic profile if the latency figures were not production measurements.
State the traffic level or request volume if available.
items.because: Latency improvements are more credible when tied to load.

items.says: Verify whether the cache introduced correctness or staleness tradeoffs worth mentioning.
Clarify whether two weeks and three days refer to total release lead time, engineering effort, or waiting time.
State whether the regression checks covered model quality, performance, compatibility, or all three.
Make the individual contribution clear if the pipeline was maintained rather than designed.
items.because: The release-cycle improvement should not be over-attributed.

items.says: Split the migration, logging-library work, onboarding, weekend on-call, and backlog result into at least two bullets.
items.because: The bullet combines too many technical, people, and operational responsibilities.

items.says: Explain why the event queue eliminated the backlog.
items.because: The causal connection is not immediately clear.

items.says: Add queue scale such as events per day, fleet size, or peak throughput if available.
Avoid implying that the logging rewrite, onboarding, and on-call work all caused the backlog result unless each contributed.
Clarify whether “800+ sensor signals per case” means features, measurements, channels, or time-series inputs.
Add the original backlog size or case count if available.
items.because: Readers need scale in addition to the 68% reduction.

items.says: State whether the reduction used a stable baseline and whether other process changes occurred during the same period.
Clarify whether the branch was built independently or as part of a team.
Define “diagnostic accuracy.”
items.because: It could mean classification accuracy, exact-match diagnosis, top-k accuracy, or another domain metric.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,200 held-out cases were never used during model or adapter development.
Make the underlying “domain adapter” method technically identifiable.
items.because: The term is somewhat ambiguous.

items.says: Explain whether the tool-use trajectories were validated manually, automatically, or by experts.
Keep “assistant-only loss masking” only when the targeted jobs value implementation-level LLM training detail.
items.because: Otherwise it may consume space without improving recruiter comprehension.

items.says: Report uncertainty or repeated-run results if possible.
items.because: The eight-point gain should not appear to come from one favorable evaluation.

items.says: “Single-request inference” conflicts with “dynamic batching” unless batching occurred across concurrent requests.
items.because: Dynamic batching normally helps under concurrent load rather than for an isolated request with no batching opportunity.

items.says: Specify whether latency was measured under concurrency, sustained traffic, or a single-user benchmark.
Include the before-and-after latency values if space permits.
State whether accuracy or output quality stayed within an accepted tolerance after INT8 quantization.
Identify the edge hardware or hardware class if relevant.
items.because: Inference performance is hardware-dependent.

items.says: The introductory clause has no clear subject performing the reduction.
Clarify how GRPO training reduced end-to-end latency.
items.because: The likely mechanism of fewer tool calls or more efficient trajectories is only implicit.

items.says: Provide before-and-after latency values.
items.because: A 5% result is modest and may not justify such a dense bullet.

items.says: Report whether accuracy, citation validity, and task completion were maintained or improved.
Remove the bullet if the result was not statistically or operationally meaningful.
items.because: It is one of the densest bullets and has one of the weakest outcomes.

items.says: Define the evaluation workload.
items.because: End-to-end agent latency varies substantially by task and tool response time.

items.says: A single rollout per prompt may not provide the within-prompt relative signal required by standard GRPO.
items.because: Standard GRPO relies on comparing a group of rollouts.

items.says: “A single rollout per prompt” conflicts with the previous bullet’s “grouped tool-use rollouts.”
State clearly whether the comparison group was formed across prompts, trajectories, or batches.
Change “Stabilised” to the US spelling for consistency.
Quantify stabilization with divergence, variance, failed runs, reward collapse, or training restarts.
items.because: The bullet currently describes a method but demonstrates no benefit.

items.says: Add the number or type of reviewers who adopted the runbook if that provides meaningful scale.
Add an effect such as more consistent escalation, faster reviews, or fewer incorrect auto-resolutions.
Clarify whether the rules were authored or only documented after others established them.
Clarify whether the project is open-source, academic, personal, or an internal platform.
Replace the vague role label “Owner” with whether the project was founded, maintained, led, or independently built.
Link directly to the repository or deployed project if it is public.
“Multi-Agent Systems” is a domain rather than a technology.
items.because: The heading should list concrete frameworks, runtime, storage, or deployment tools if relevant.

items.says: Remove or substantially change the unsupported “AI-first engineering practices” bullet.
items.because: Its claims are broad and promotional.

items.says: Identify the exact practice introduced, who adopted it, and what changed.
Quantify the delivery improvement or downstream impact.
Clarify what “platform” and “downstream teams” refer to.
items.because: This is especially unclear if the work is a personal project without organizational users.

items.says: Reducing latency from 900 ms to 600 ms is approximately a 33% reduction, not 50%.
Clarify whether cached results could become stale and how cache validity was handled.
Explain the benchmark conditions, including concurrency and cache-hit rate.
Distinguish tool-result caching from reusing completed sub-agent answers if they were separate mechanisms.
Confirm that both p95 figures used the same workload and hardware.
The gain from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not 12%.
items.because: The relative improvement is approximately 16.9%.

items.says: Define the benchmark suite by task count, task types, and whether it is public or custom.
Clarify how task completion was scored and whether the improvement held across multiple runs.
Mention any latency or cost tradeoff caused by retries.
items.because: Retries often improve success at the expense of both.

items.says: Explain safeguards against repeatedly retrying invalid or unrecoverable sub-agent calls.
Clarify the project’s affiliation and provide a repository or contribution link if public.
Ensure the contribution history substantiates the scope implied by “Contributor.”
Verify that all eight metrics were accepted upstream and currently run by default.
Name the metric categories or evaluation dimensions if “citation and faithfulness” is not sufficiently clear.
Name or link the recognizable project instead of describing it generically.
Distinguish metrics that were designed from metrics that were only implemented.
Specify the Kendall statistic used, such as tau or tau-b.
Explain what was ranked and what the evaluator’s scores were compared against.
Clarify whether the 400+ trials were independent and how many original reports were used.
Describe the degradation levels or severity ordering.
items.because: That context is needed to establish that 0.89 is meaningful.

items.says: Include statistical uncertainty or significance if available.
Clarify what “defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling” means operationally.
Explain the impact of each defect or at least the most important one.
items.because: The current categories are abstract.

items.says: Rewrite “to their modules” to make the debugging scope and root-cause identification clearer.
items.because: The phrase is difficult to parse.

items.says: Link the relevant issues or pull requests if the fixes were accepted upstream.
Quantify the improvement after the fixes if it was measured.
Git should not be listed under “Programming.”
items.because: It is a development tool, not a programming language.

items.says: Kubernetes should not be listed under “ML & Agents.”
items.because: It belongs in a tools, infrastructure, cloud, or deployment category.

items.says: The category mixes training techniques, libraries, domains, and infrastructure.
items.because: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, and Kubernetes are not the same type of skill.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific.
items.because: The project bullets demonstrate more precise evaluation capabilities.

items.says: Consider adding evidenced technologies such as CI/CD, event queues, caching, model serving, quantization, or observability when the actual tools can be named.
Avoid listing GRPO while the corresponding bullets remain technically ambiguous.
